Recipes Heptane glue Mix the tape and heptane for 3 h in a rocker. Discard the tape and use the liquid for downstream applications. Store the heptane glue in a dropper bottle. Embryo collection plates Dissolve the agar and brown sugar in 250 mL of water and autoclave. Add 250 mL of apple juice, mix, and add the Nipagin solution. Pour into 6 cm Petri dishes and store at 4 °C. Before using, add yeast paste (dried yeast dissolved in water). Punch small holes on the base of the plastic beakers. These will contain the flies, and the Petri dish with yeast will serve as a lid of the embryo collection cage. Embryo basket Make an open-ended 5 cm cylinder by cutting the conical tube using a cutter knife. Cut a round window on the lid of the conical tube. Cut the metallic mesh into a circle that fits inside the lid. Screw in the lid containing the metallic mesh back into the conical tube.

steps.title: Prepare heptane glue
steps.instruction: Mix double‑sided tape with heptane in a container and place on a rocker for 3 h; discard the tape, keep the liquid, and store the heptane glue in a dropper bottle for later use.

steps.title: Prepare embryo collection plates
steps.instruction: Dissolve 10 g agar and 4.2 g brown sugar in 250 mL distilled water, autoclave, then add 250 mL apple juice, mix, and add 5 mL 10 % Nipagin (in EtOH); pour the mixture into 6 cm Petri dishes, store at 4 °C, and before use add yeast paste made from dried yeast dissolved in water. Punch small holes in the base of 100 mL plastic beakers that will hold the flies; the yeast‑coated Petri dish will serve as the lid of the embryo collection cage.

steps.title: Assemble embryo basket
steps.instruction: Cut a 5 cm open‑ended cylinder from a 50 mL conical tube, cut a round window in the tube lid, cut a piece of 100‑wire‑per‑inch stainless‑steel mesh to fit the window, and screw the lid with the mesh back onto the tube to form the embryo basket.

steps.title: Set up embryo collection cages
steps.instruction: At least three days before the experiment, transfer flies of the desired genotype into a 100 mL plastic beaker, cover the beaker with a prepared embryo collection plate, and replace the plate daily to allow flies to adapt and to accumulate eggs.

steps.title: Collect embryos overnight
steps.instruction: One day before the experiment, let the flies lay eggs in the cages for 16–24 h (overnight), then replace the used embryo plate with a fresh one.

steps.title: Dechorionate embryos with bleach
steps.instruction: Add enough 50 % commercial bleach (in water) to the agar surface of the embryo plate to fully cover the embryos; incubate for 1–2 min until the chorionic membrane is completely dissolved (verify under a dissection scope and optionally waggling the plate). Wear gloves and a lab coat.

steps.title: Wash and transfer dechorionated embryos
steps.instruction: Immediately transfer the dechorionated embryos to the embryo basket, wash the basket several times with distilled water using a wash bottle, then rinse abundantly with tap water; confirm removal of bleach by the absence of odor. Using a paintbrush, move the washed embryos to a new embryo collection plate pre‑warmed to room temperature.

steps.title: Select stage‑15 embryos
steps.instruction: Under a dissecting microscope, pick embryos that are approximately stage 15 (dorsal side up, yolk with irregular anterior/posterior edges); perform this step quickly to avoid heating from the microscope light.

steps.title: Mount embryos – one‑by‑one method
steps.instruction: Pour two drops of heptane glue onto a glass‑bottom imaging plate and let the heptane evaporate. Using a paintbrush, transfer ~5 stage‑15 embryos onto the dried glue with the region of interest facing downwards, then add enough halocarbon oil 27 to completely cover the embryos (do not dispense oil directly onto the embryos). Mount quickly to prevent dehydration.

steps.title: Mount embryos – all‑at‑once method
steps.instruction: Pour two drops of heptane glue onto an imaging plate and let the heptane evaporate. Using forceps, select 5–10 stage‑15 embryos, align them with the region of interest facing upwards, and cut a cube of agar containing the embryos with a scalpel blade #23. Realign if necessary, invert the imaging plate (glue side down) and place it onto the agar cube so the embryos adhere to the glass. Position the agar cube on a raised surface (e.g., a nail‑polish bottle) to avoid pressure on the embryos. Add enough halocarbon oil 27 to fully cover the embryos, avoiding direct oil contact with the embryos themselves.

steps.title: Calibrate two‑photon laser settings
steps.instruction: In the confocal microscope, set the excitation wavelength to 950 nm (two‑photon mode). Start with 75 % laser power and 8 iterations; if tissue damage (autofluorescence or permanent deformation) is observed, halve the number of iterations until damage disappears. If the power is insufficient, increase iterations or power until a clean ablation is achieved without excessive bleaching.

steps.title: Acquire pre‑cut Z‑stack and define ROI
steps.instruction: Focus on the selected embryo, acquire a Z‑stack still image of the cell or tissue to document the initial condition, then define a region of interest (ROI) where the laser cut will be performed using the bleaching module.

steps.title: Perform laser cut and record recoil
steps.instruction: Adjust the bleaching module so that the laser cut occurs after five imaging frames, then continue acquiring ~50 post‑cut frames (total acquisition ≈ 90 s) with the fastest possible rate, limiting the interval to a maximum of one image every 10 s. This captures the recoil and its plateau phase.

steps.title: Acquire post‑cut Z‑stack and save data
steps.instruction: Immediately after the recoil acquisition, acquire another Z‑stack still image to record the final morphology, then save all images in a lossless format such as .tiff, .lsm, .lif, or .nd2.
